q01: This course is designed for beginners aiming to learn data science within a 6-month period, covering essential topics such as statistical analysis, machine learning algorithms, data visualization, and database management. Participants will gain hands-on experience with Python or R programming languages and tools like SQL, Pandas, and Matplotlib, preparing them to analyze and interpret complex data sets effectively.
q02: This course path focuses on machine learning and deep learning techniques using Python, suitable for learners with a basic understanding of programming. The path spans approximately 12 weeks and covers essential skills including data preprocessing, model training, evaluation metrics, neural network architectures, and practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.
q03: This course covers full-stack web development using Python and JavaScript, suitable for intermediate-level learners with some programming experience. The course is designed to last approximately 12 weeks and will provide hands-on training in backend development with Python frameworks like Flask or Django, frontend development with JavaScript and popular libraries such as React or Angular, database management, and deployment strategies. Students will gain proficiency in building dynamic, interactive web applications from both client-side and server-side perspectives.
q04: This course focuses on advanced cybersecurity, network defense, and ethical hacking techniques, suitable for intermediate-level learners with a basic understanding of computer networks and security concepts. The course is designed to last approximately 12 weeks and will cover key topics including network architecture, threat analysis, secure coding practices, intrusion detection systems, and hands-on experience with ethical hacking tools and methodologies. Students will develop skills in identifying vulnerabilities, implementing defensive strategies, and conducting ethical hacking assessments to protect network infrastructure.
q05: This course covers cloud computing infrastructure and DevOps deployment, suitable for intermediate-level learners with basic knowledge of cloud services and scripting. The course is designed to last approximately 12 weeks and will provide hands-on experience in setting up and managing cloud environments, automating deployments using CI/CD pipelines, and implementing DevOps best practices. Key topics include cloud architecture, virtual machines, containerization with Docker, orchestration with Kubernetes, and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) strategies.
cs06: This course is designed for intermediate-level backend developers aiming to transition into data engineering roles, focusing on SQL and Apache Spark. Over the course of 12 weeks, learners will master essential data engineering concepts, including database design and management, ETL processes, big data processing with Spark, and data warehousing techniques. Key skills developed include advanced SQL querying, Spark programming, and hands-on experience with data pipelines and distributed computing environments.
cs07: This course is designed for beginners with no prior programming experience and aims to teach mobile app development, focusing initially on Android apps. The course will span approximately 12 weeks and covers essential skills such as understanding Android Studio, Java and Kotlin programming languages, user interface design, and basic app functionality. Key topics include creating simple applications, integrating APIs, and deploying apps to the Google Play Store.
cs08: This course is designed for intermediate-level learners who wish to gain a comprehensive understanding of relational database management systems, including relational database design principles, effective indexing strategies, and techniques for query optimization and tuning. The course spans approximately 4 weeks and covers essential topics such as normalization, schema design, index selection and maintenance, and performance analysis and improvement through query tuning.
math01: This course is designed for learners looking to relearn calculus with a focus on foundational concepts essential for an engineering degree. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of algebra and trigonometry. The course, which spans approximately 8 weeks, covers key topics such as limits, derivatives, integrals, and their applications, providing a solid mathematical foundation necessary for advanced engineering studies.
math02: This course is designed for intermediate-level learners with a background in linear algebra and basic probability theory, aiming to equip students with the necessary skills to understand and follow advanced machine learning papers. The course will cover key topics including vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, probability distributions, random variables, and statistical inference, spanning approximately 12 weeks of study.
math03: This course is designed for intermediate-level learners who wish to gain a solid understanding of statistical methods for interpreting research studies, without focusing on programming. The course will span approximately 8 weeks and will cover essential topics such as descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and data visualization, equipping students with the skills to critically analyze and interpret research findings effectively.
math04: This course is designed for beginners in computer science and covers fundamental topics in discrete mathematics and logic, including set theory, logic gates, Boolean algebra, and graph theory. Prerequisites include basic algebra skills. The course is structured to last approximately 12 weeks, providing a comprehensive introduction to the mathematical foundations essential for computer science, with a focus on developing logical reasoning and problem-solving skills.
math05: This course is designed for students with a solid foundation in high school algebra who wish to advance to the study of differential equations. Over a period of approximately 12 weeks, participants will develop their understanding through a series of modules that cover essential precalculus topics, such as functions, trigonometry, and exponential functions, before progressing to the core concepts of differential equations including first-order and second-order equations, Laplace transforms, and systems of differential equations. By the end of the course, learners will be equipped with the necessary mathematical tools and problem-solving skills to tackle advanced problems in calculus and related fields.
biz01: This course is designed for intermediate-level learners who wish to gain a comprehensive understanding of financial accounting to effectively read and interpret a company's annual report. The course will span approximately 8 weeks and covers key topics including financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement), accounting principles, financial ratios analysis, and industry-specific financial reporting standards. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze financial statements, understand the implications of various accounting choices, and perform basic financial ratio analyses to assess a company's financial health.
biz02: This course is designed for small business owners looking to enhance their digital marketing and social media strategies. Prerequisites include basic computer literacy and an understanding of internet basics. The course, which spans approximately 8 weeks, covers essential topics such as creating a social media content calendar, leveraging platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, implementing SEO techniques, and analyzing campaign performance using analytics tools. Students will develop skills in managing social media accounts, crafting engaging content, and measuring the effectiveness of digital marketing efforts.
biz03: This course is designed for beginners looking to start their own company and covers essential entrepreneurship and fundraising fundamentals, including business planning, market analysis, financial management, and pitching to investors. The course, which spans approximately 8 weeks, will equip learners with the necessary skills to develop a solid business idea, create a comprehensive business plan, and effectively raise capital through various funding strategies. Key topics include identifying market opportunities, developing a value proposition, creating financial projections, and mastering the art of investor presentations.
biz04: This course covers project management fundamentals through to agile methodologies, designed for beginners with no prior experience in project management. The course spans approximately 12 weeks and includes topics such as project planning, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and agile practices like Scrum and Kanban. Students will develop essential skills in project initiation, scope definition, time and cost management, and agile team leadership.
biz05: This course is designed for individuals looking to transition into a career in banking, focusing on corporate finance and investment analysis. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of financial concepts and mathematics. The course, which spans approximately 12 weeks, covers key topics such as financial statement analysis, valuation techniques, capital budgeting, risk management, and portfolio theory, equipping students with essential skills for a career in banking.
biz06: This course is designed for individuals seeking to enhance their understanding of supply chain and operations management specifically for manufacturing roles, targeting intermediate-level professionals. The course will span approximately 12 weeks and covers key areas including demand forecasting, inventory management, production planning, quality control, and supply chain optimization, equipping students with the necessary skills to improve operational efficiency and effectiveness in manufacturing environments.
health01: This course, designed for beginners with no prior nutritional knowledge required, spans approximately 4 weeks and focuses on understanding nutrition and healthy eating based on solid scientific evidence. Key topics include macronutrients and micronutrients, dietary guidelines, evidence-based nutrition research, and practical strategies for maintaining a balanced diet. Students will develop skills in interpreting nutritional information, evaluating health claims, and applying evidence-based practices to their own eating habits.
health02: This course provides an introduction to public health and epidemiology fundamentals, suitable for individuals with no clinical background. Over a period of 8 weeks, learners will gain essential knowledge in epidemiological methods, public health principles, and the impact of diseases on populations. Key topics include disease surveillance, risk factors, outbreak investigation, and public health interventions, equipping participants with the skills to understand and contribute to public health initiatives.
health03: This course provides an introduction to psychology and mental health, designed for support workers at an intermediate level. Over a duration of 12 weeks, participants will explore key psychological theories, mental health disorders, and effective support strategies. Specific skills covered include understanding cognitive-behavioral principles, recognizing signs of mental health issues, and developing communication and intervention techniques for supporting individuals with mental health needs.
health04: This course provides an in-depth study of human anatomy and physiology, designed as essential preparation for students entering a nursing program. Prerequisites include basic high school science knowledge. The course spans approximately 12 weeks and covers key topics such as cell biology, tissue organization, organ systems, and physiological processes, equipping students with the foundational knowledge necessary for advanced nursing studies.
health05: This course provides an in-depth exploration of global health systems and healthcare policy, suitable for intermediate learners with a basic understanding of public health or healthcare administration. Spanning approximately 12 weeks, the course covers key topics including the structure and function of health systems worldwide, the impact of healthcare policies on population health outcomes, financing mechanisms, and ethical considerations. Students will develop skills in analyzing health system performance, evaluating healthcare policies, and understanding the global determinants of health.
comm01: This course is designed for beginners and early-level speakers aiming to develop confidence in public speaking and presenting. Over a duration of 8 weeks, participants will learn essential skills such as effective communication, audience engagement, speech organization, and delivery techniques. Key topics include understanding your audience, overcoming stage fright, using visual aids effectively, and crafting compelling narratives.
